tasks.title: Tailwind CSS 4 업그레이드 및 스타터 정리
tasks.description: Upgrade Tailwind CSS from 3.4.1 to v4, migrate theme tokens to @theme inline, replace tailwindcss-animate with tw-animate-css, and remove starter template components
tasks.details:
1. Install Tailwind CSS v4 dependencies:
   npm install tailwindcss@next @tailwindcss/postcss@next
   npm uninstall autoprefixer tailwindcss-animate
   npm install tw-animate-css

2. Migrate tailwind.config.ts to app/globals.css:
   - Move theme.extend.colors to @theme inline block
   - Move borderRadius tokens to CSS variables
   - Keep darkMode as @custom-variant dark
   - Delete tailwind.config.ts after migration

3. Update postcss.config.mjs:
   module.exports = {
     plugins: {
       '@tailwindcss/postcss': {}
     }
   }

4. Verify components.json has empty tailwind.config value

5. Remove starter components:
   - components/tutorial/** (all files)
   - components/hero.tsx

   - components/supabase-logo.tsx

subtasks.details: Run `npm install zod sonner` to add both dependencies to the project. Zod will be used for input validation in Server Actions, and sonner provides the toast notification system for user feedback on save/delete operations.

subtasks.title: Create lib/actions/links.ts with createLink Server Action
subtasks.description: Implement the createLink Server Action with zod schema validation, user authentication check, Supabase insert, and revalidatePath
subtasks.details: Create lib/actions/links.ts with 'use server' directive. Define createLinkSchema using zod to validate url (must be valid URL), title (min 1 char), and optional fields (thumbnail_url, description, tags array, memo). Implement createLink function that: (1) validates input with zod, (2) gets authenticated user via createClient().auth.getUser(), (3) returns error if not authenticated, (4) inserts row into links table with user_id, (5) calls revalidatePath('/links'), (6) returns ActionResult with success/error. Handle zod validation errors separately from database errors.
subtasks.testStrategy: TypeScript compilation check. Manual test by temporarily calling the action from a test page with valid/invalid inputs to verify zod error messages appear correctly.

subtasks.title: Implement deleteLink Server Action with RLS backup
subtasks.description: Add deleteLink Server Action to lib/actions/links.ts with user authentication and RLS backup check
subtasks.details: In lib/actions/links.ts, implement deleteLink(id: string) that: (1) gets authenticated user, (2) returns error if not authenticated, (3) calls supabase.from('links').delete().eq('id', id).eq('user_id', user.id) to ensure RLS backup (only delete own links), (4) calls revalidatePath('/links'), (5) returns ActionResult. Catch and return generic error message on failure.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manual test by attempting to delete another user's link (should fail silently due to RLS). Verify successful deletion triggers revalidation.

tasks.description: Perform end-to-end integration testing of entire user journey from signup to search/filter/toggle/delete, verify edge cases, and document any regressions
tasks.details:
This is a comprehensive QA task using Playwright MCP to validate all features work together correctly.

1. Create test scenarios document: tests/e2e-scenarios.md

2. Test full user journey:
   - Start from landing page
   - Sign up new account
   - Login
   - Verify redirect to /links
   - See empty state
   - Save first link with metadata
   - Save second link (metadata fail → manual)
   - Add tags and memo
   - Toggle read/favorite
   - Search and filter
   - Delete link
   - Logout

3. Edge cases:
   - Very long title (300+ chars)
   - Very long URL (1000+ chars)
   - Link with no tags
   - Link with no memo
   - Special characters in search (unicode, emoji)
   - Thumbnail load failure (broken image)
   - Invalid image URL

4. Error scenarios:
   - Network timeout during metadata fetch
   - Server Action failure (simulate DB error)
   - Concurrent updates (2 tabs, toggle same link)
   - Invalid URL formats

5. Security checks:
   - Non-authenticated access to /links → redirect
   - RLS enforcement (cannot access other user's links)
   - XSS attempt in search query
   - SQL injection attempt in search

6. Performance:
   - Page load time for 100+ links
   - Search response time
   - Optimistic update responsiveness

7. Accessibility:
   - Keyboard navigation (Tab, Enter, Esc)
   - Screen reader labels (aria-label)
   - Focus management in dialogs

Document all failures in respective task files for regression fixes.

tasks.details:
Background: types/profile.ts (Profile interface) and the PROFILES_TABLE_DDL draft in types/database.ts were already created as documentation-only work (see docs/ROADMAP.md Task 003-1, docs/PRD.md sections 6 and 9). This task covers the actual migration execution, which was intentionally deferred.

1. Apply migration using mcp__supabase__apply_migration, executing the SQL already drafted in types/database.ts (PROFILES_TABLE_DDL):
   - CREATE TABLE public.profiles (id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade, display_name text, avatar_url text, created_at timestamptz default now(), updated_at timestamptz default now())
   - handle_profiles_updated_at() trigger function + on_profiles_updated BEFORE UPDATE trigger
   - handle_new_user() SECURITY DEFINER trigger function reading raw_user_meta_data ->> 'display_name' / ->> 'avatar_url', fired AFTER INSERT ON auth.users as on_auth_user_created
   - ALTER TABLE public.profiles ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
   - CREATE POLICY "Users can view own profile" ON public.profiles FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = id)
   - CREATE POLICY "Users can update own profile" ON public.profiles FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = id)
   - Deliberately no anon SELECT grant (unlike the Supabase official managing-user-data example) and no insert/delete policies (row creation is handled by the trigger, deletion cascades from auth.users ON DELETE CASCADE).

2. Run this in the same session as Task 8's links migration so both schema changes land together.

3. Regenerate Supabase types (types/database.types.ts) after both migrations run, and verify types/profile.ts stays consistent with the generated schema.
tasks.testStrategy: Use mcp__supabase__execute_sql or Supabase Studio to verify: (1) profiles table created with correct schema. (2) RLS enabled and only the two own-row policies exist (no anon grant). (3) Sign up a new test user and confirm a matching profiles row is auto-created by the trigger with display_name/avatar_url null. (4) Update the row via the authenticated client and confirm updated_at changes automatically. (5) Confirm a second test user cannot select/update the first user's profile row.
tasks.expansionPrompt: Break into: (1) Apply Supabase migration via mcp__supabase__apply_migration executing the PROFILES_TABLE_DDL from types/database.ts, including the profiles table creation, updated_at trigger function and trigger, handle_new_user() SECURITY DEFINER trigger reading raw_user_meta_data, and RLS enablement with own-row policies (no anon grant), (2) Verify migration success and run alongside Task 8's links migration in the same session so both schema changes land together, (3) Regenerate Supabase types using mcp__supabase__generate_typescript_types, save to types/database.types.ts, and ensure types/profile.ts stays consistent with generated schema, (4) Test trigger behavior by signing up a new test user and verifying auto-created profiles row, test updated_at trigger by updating a profile row, and verify RLS with 2 test users to confirm isolation.

tasks.description: Define the Profile TypeScript interface and draft the public.profiles table DDL (table, updated_at trigger, handle_new_user() auth sync trigger, RLS policy comments) following the Supabase managing-user-data guide, scoped to LinkLink's single-user needs. Actual migration execution is deferred to Task 17.
tasks.details:
Proposed by the user, referencing the Supabase official managing-user-data guide (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/managing-user-data). Confirmed before implementing that the project had zero profile footprint: no types/ profile file, no supabase/migrations directory, sign-up form collects only email/password (no options.data metadata), and PRD only defined the links table.

1. types/profile.ts: added the Profile interface (id, display_name, avatar_url, created_at, updated_at).

2. types/database.ts: added PROFILES_TABLE_DDL alongside the existing LINKS_TABLE_DDL, containing:
   - CREATE TABLE public.profiles (id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade, display_name text, avatar_url text, created_at timestamptz default now(), updated_at timestamptz default now())
   - handle_profiles_updated_at() trigger function + on_profiles_updated BEFORE UPDATE trigger
   - handle_new_user() SECURITY DEFINER trigger function reading raw_user_meta_data ->> 'display_name' / ->> 'avatar_url', fired AFTER INSERT ON auth.users as on_auth_user_created
   - RLS policy comments (own-row select/update only, deliberately no anon SELECT grant and no insert/delete policies) — actual ALTER TABLE/CREATE POLICY execution left for Task 17

3. docs/PRD.md: added a '### profiles' subsection under section 6 (데이터 모델) with the column table, and a `[가정]` bullet under section 9 explaining this is an infrastructure addition not mapped to any F001-F007 feature, and that it deliberately omits the official guide's anon SELECT grant since LinkLink is single-user.

4. docs/ROADMAP.md: inserted a 'Task 003-1: profiles 테이블 및 사용자 데이터 동기화 트리거 설계 (제안)' entry between Task 003 and Task 004, marked done (✅).

Design decisions that intentionally diverge from the official Supabase example: display_name/avatar_url columns instead of first_name/last_name (no name-collection UI exists yet); added created_at/updated_at for auditability; RLS restricted to auth.uid() = id (no anon grant, no public profile directory concept); no insert/delete policies since the trigger owns creation and auth.users ON DELETE CASCADE owns deletion.
tasks.testStrategy: TypeScript compilation check: `npx tsc --noEmit` run and passed after adding types/profile.ts and the PROFILES_TABLE_DDL export. No runtime testing needed — this task is type/documentation-only, matching Task 3's testStrategy pattern. Runtime verification (RLS, trigger behavior) happens in Task 17 once the migration is actually applied.
